transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, uh, thanks for seeing me. What brings me in... I guess it's mostly work stuff. I work retail, you know, over at the big box store on Route 9? They've got me in the back mostly these days, organizing the stockroom. Which is fine, usually. I mean, my buddy Dave works back there too, and we get along great. We actually went fishing last weekend up at the lake, didn't catch much, but it was nice to get out, you know? But anyway, the stockroom... it's just, what brings me in is that the second I think there might be a bat or something flapping around back there, my heart just jumps right out of my chest. I start sweating buckets, and I just feel like I need to get out of there right that second. It's awful. Dave thinks it's funny, but I can't stand it. We had this one time at the lake where a bird flew by, and I almost dropped my rod, but... yeah, the stockroom is where it really hits me.
Do you ever feel this same kind of panic or anxiety in other situations, like in crowded places, when you're alone, or during stressful moments at work?

No, not really. Crowds don't bother me at all. Actually, I kind of like them. Like, last month, my buddy Dave and I went down to the city for this huge outdoor concert. There must have been thousands of people there, shoulder to shoulder. We were right up near the front, too. It was a tribute band for classic rock, you know, Zeppelin, AC/DC, that kind of stuff. The lead guitarist was incredible, he had this vintage Gibson that just screamed. We ended up getting some terrible hot dogs from a cart afterwards, but man, it was a great time. I didn't feel anxious at all, just had a blast. And being alone is fine, too. I live by myself, well, just me and my iguana, Iggy. He's a trip, honestly. He mostly just sits under his heat lamp all day, but sometimes he'll bob his head at me when I walk by. So yeah, it's really just... just the bats, or anything that flaps like that. If it's not that, I'm pretty much fine.
